objective: Audit and normalize all GLPI business data imported from IT_Management_System.xlsm so every supported entity uses clean GLPI-native display fields, structured references, stable source keys, valid relationships, and idempotent importer behavior.

in: Imported GLPI business records and supporting references in the running glpi database
Users, groups, memberships, printers, peripherals/provisions, tickets, actors, locations, manufacturers, models, states, and categories
Transactional cleanup and deterministic integrity verification
out: GLPI framework, migration, session, log, plugin-internal, and authentication-secret data
Fabricating source details absent from both the database and repository
Deleting historical tickets or inactive users solely because of status

constraints: Preserve source keys in registration_number, externalid, and otherserial.
Use transactions and preserve record IDs and relationships.
Do not guess missing provision details.
Remove prefixes and placeholders only from user-facing fields when structured/source fields retain the information.
Keep asset names meaningful and unique while storing manufacturer, model, location, state, owner, and contact separately.
Make importer reruns preserve normalized structure and friendly names.
Do not expose credentials in tracked files or reports.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A deterministic audit covers every imported business-record family, counts, display anomalies, placeholders, duplicates, missing relationships, and source-key coverage.
Imported users, groups, memberships, and reference entities have clean display values, valid relationships, stable source IDs, and no redundant import prefixes.
Printers and peripherals use the best available friendly names and structured manufacturer, model, location, state, owner, and contact fields without invented details.
Imported tickets retain history and source IDs while actors, categories, statuses, priorities, dates, and titles are structurally valid and free of redundant import labels.
The importer is idempotent and does not recreate removed prefixes, placeholders, duplicate references, or overwritten friendly names.
Final verification shows referential integrity, unique source keys, no targeted display anomalies, valid PHP syntax, and explicit review evidence.

assessment.reason: This changes live relational business data and the importer that can overwrite it; incorrect mappings could silently corrupt ownership, history, or reference relationships.
surfaces: Imported users, profiles, groups, and memberships
Printers, peripherals, references, ownership, and location
Tickets, actors, categories, statuses, and dates
unknowns: The original workbook is unavailable, so missing provision details cannot be reconstructed.
Some source terminology and future dates may be intentional.
Contextual duplicate labels may be valid in GLPI.

practices.practice: Inventory before mutation and classify safe versus ambiguous normalization.
practices.reason: A complete baseline is required before broad cleanup.

practices.practice: Apply deterministic SQL mappings transactionally with post-change invariants.
practices.reason: Relational changes must preserve IDs and relationships.

practices.practice: Align importer behavior with normalized structure and validate repeatability.
practices.reason: Future imports must not undo cleanup.

practices.practice: Run full integrity checks and source-bound reviews.
practices.reason: Broad cleanup needs current machine and review evidence.

obligations.text: Inventory imported families, source keys, anomalies, placeholders, duplicates, and missing relationships.
Normalize users, groups, memberships, and reference displays transactionally and verify relationship invariants.
Normalize assets, provisions, tickets, and actors transactionally and verify relationship and history invariants.
Validate importer syntax and normalized lookup/write behavior without destructive re-import.
Run final cross-entity invariants and complete explicit source-bound and independent reviews.

Transactional mappings are checked with before-and-after invariants.

args: PW=$(podman inspect glpi-db --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | awk -F= '$1=="MARIADB_PASSWORD"{print substr($0,index($0,"=")+1)}') && podman exec -i -e MYSQL_PWD="$PW" glpi-db mariadb -uglpi glpi --batch --raw --skip-column-names -e "SELECT CONCAT('IMPORTED_USERS=',COUNT(*),', DUP_KEYS=',COUNT(*)-COUNT(DISTINCT registration_number),', SOURCE_PREFIX_LOGINS=',SUM(name LIKE 'itms-%'),', RECORD_SURNAMES=',SUM(realname='Record')) FROM glpi_users WHERE registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP:%' OR registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP-HASH:%'; SELECT CONCAT('SYNTHETIC_EMAILS=',COUNT(*)) FROM glpi_useremails ue JOIN glpi_users u ON u.id=ue.users_id WHERE (u.registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP:%' OR u.registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP-HASH:%') AND ue.email LIKE '%@employees.invalid'; SELECT CONCAT('GROUP_PREFIXES=',COUNT(*),', GROUP_COUNT=',(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM glpi_groups WHERE comment='Imported department from IT_Management_System.xlsm')) FROM glpi_groups WHERE name LIKE 'ITMS:%'; SELECT CONCAT('CATEGORY_PREFIXES=',COUNT(*)) FROM glpi_itilcategories WHERE name LIKE 'ITMS:%'; SELECT CONCAT('USERS_WITHOUT_PROFILE=',COUNT(*)) FROM glpi_users u WHERE (u.registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP:%' OR u.registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP-HASH:%') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM glpi_profiles_users pu WHERE pu.users_id=u.id); SELECT CONCAT('USERS_WITHOUT_GROUP=',COUNT(*)) FROM glpi_users u WHERE (u.registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP:%' OR u.registration_number LIKE 'ITMS-EMP-HASH:%') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM glpi_groups_users gu JOIN glpi_groups g ON g.id=gu.groups_id AND g.comment='Imported department from IT_Management_System.xlsm' WHERE gu.users_id=u.id); SELECT CONCAT('NORMALIZED_COLLISIONS=',COUNT(*)) FROM (SELECT LOWER(TRIM(name)) n FROM glpi_groups GROUP BY n HAVING COUNT(*)>1 UNION ALL SELECT LOWER(TRIM(name)) n FROM glpi_itilcategories GROUP BY n HAVING COUNT(*)>1) d;"

evidence.summary: Model self-review of the transactional organizational cleanup and current audit evidence found all 74 imported users retain unique dedicated source keys, profiles, and imported-group memberships; five fabricated Record surnames and 29 synthetic invalid emails were removed; 16 group and 9 category display prefixes were normalized without collisions; no unrelated records were targeted.

]

decisions.text: Interpret all data as all imported GLPI business data and supporting references, not GLPI internal tables.
decisions.basis: This satisfies the cleanup request without corrupting application internals.

decisions.text: Preserve dedicated source identifiers while removing redundant prefixes from display fields.
decisions.basis: Source keys are required for traceability and idempotency.

decisions.text: Do not fabricate missing peripheral details.
decisions.basis: The workbook is unavailable and current records lack recoverable values.

risks.text: Incorrect ownership or actor remapping could alter accountability.
risks.mitigation: Use source keys, existing names, and IDs; leave ambiguous mappings unchanged.

risks.text: Importer reruns could revert cleanup or duplicate references.
risks.mitigation: Normalize importer behavior and preserve friendly names.
Limit changes to stable fields, update timestamps, use transactions, and verify invariants.
